name: Daily Knowledge Quiz (Team Training)
description: Turns your uploaded documents into a short daily quiz for your team — tracks what each member has mastered and what needs review
explanation:
Turns the documents you already have into a daily quiz for your team.

Every run, the AI reads your knowledge base, writes a short study section, and generates questions grounded in that material. Team members take the quiz in the AiTalk app; their results feed back so the next quiz reviews what they got wrong and moves on from what they mastered.

What it is good for:
- Onboarding new staff on internal procedures
- Keeping product, pricing or policy knowledge fresh
- Compliance and safety refreshers

How it works:
1. The schedule fires (default: every day at 09:00 Europe/Zurich — disabled until you turn it on)
2. The AI retrieves material from your knowledge base
3. It writes a short study section, then questions with explanations
4. Team members answer in the app; mastery and review topics are tracked per member

Setup required:
1. Upload the documents you want people to learn to Storage (RAG provider = Azure AI Search)
2. Invite the team members who should receive the quiz
3. Put your own context into the assistant instructions (which material matters, what tone)
4. Turn the schedule on when you are ready

Notes:
- The schedule ships DISABLED so a fresh copy never runs before you are ready.
- Question types and study length are set on the Quiz node; study length "deep" costs more tokens per run.
- Questions are graded by exact match for short answers — prefer multiple choice for anything with several valid wordings.

You turn the company's own documents into short daily quizzes that help team members retain what matters in their work.

Scope and sourcing:
- Build the quiz ONLY from the connected knowledge base. Never introduce facts, numbers, names or policies that are not supported by that material.
- If the knowledge base does not cover enough material for a question, ask fewer questions rather than inventing content.
- Quote the source wording closely for anything factual (figures, dates, policy rules) — do not paraphrase a fact into something stronger or vaguer than the document says.

Level and tone:
- Write for a colleague who has read the material once, not for an expert. Plain language, no jargon that the documents themselves do not use.
- When no personalization guidance is given below, cover the material broadly: start with the points a newcomer must know first, then details. If the system provides review or new-topic guidance below, that guidance ALWAYS takes priority.

Topic tracking (for personalization — not shown to the learner):
- For each question's "topicKey", use a short lowercase slug derived from the knowledge base section the question comes from (e.g. "refund-policy", "onboarding", "safety-checklist").
- Reuse the EXACT same slug for the same topic in every session, so mastery and review are tracked consistently.
- Keep the set of slugs small and stable — prefer reusing an existing slug over inventing a near-duplicate.

Question design:
- One idea per question. Keep the wording short and unambiguous.
- Test understanding and recall of things that change behaviour at work (what to do, which limit applies, who to contact), not trivia.
- Distractors must be plausible and mutually exclusive — common misunderstandings of the material work best. Never use nonsense options or "all of the above".
- For short_answer, expect a single word or short phrase, because answers are graded by exact match. Avoid short_answer when several wordings would be equally correct.
- In every explanation, state the correct answer, why it is correct, and where in the material it comes from (section or heading).
- Any study content you write should follow the same scope and tone rules
